column1: Deep learning approaches have increasingly been employed to analyze high-dimensional biomedical imaging data. Recent studies demonstrate their capacity to detect subtle pathological signatures, outperforming traditional machine‑learning pipelines. Despite their promise, challenges remain in model interpretability, data scarcity, and clinical integration.

COVID‑19 pathogenesis involves a complex interplay between viral replication, host immune responses, and multi‑organ involvement. Emerging evidence highlights the role of endothelial dysfunction and cytokine dysregulation in severe disease. Continued investigation is essential for refining therapeutic strategies and improving patient outcomes.

Human connectome research aims to map the structural and functional organization of the brain at multiple scales. Recent advances in diffusion MRI and resting‑state fMRI have enabled detailed network characterization, providing insights into cognition, neurodevelopment, and neuropsychiatric disorders.

Virtual reality technologies are increasingly utilized in rehabilitation and behavioral research. Immersive environments offer controlled stimuli for motor training, phobia desensitization, and cognitive assessment. Ongoing work explores optimizing VR fidelity and minimizing cybersickness in clinical populations.

Brain–machine interfaces (BMIs) enable direct communication between neural activity and external devices. Contemporary BMIs employ high‑resolution neural decoding to restore motor function in individuals with paralysis. Research continues to improve long‑term implant stability and adaptive decoding algorithms.

Electroactive polymers (EAPs) have emerged as promising biomaterials for soft robotic actuation and biomedical device fabrication. Their tunable mechanical properties and biocompatibility support applications ranging from artificial muscles to implantable sensors. Key limitations include long‑term durability and controlled stimulus responsiveness.

PEDOT‑based electrodes are widely used in neural interfacing due to their high conductivity, low impedance, and mechanical flexibility. Advances in electrode fabrication techniques have enabled stable chronic recordings in both central and peripheral nervous systems. Further optimization focuses on improving biostability and reducing inflammatory responses.

Neuroprosthetics aims to restore lost sensory or motor function through the integration of engineered devices with neural circuitry. Recent progress includes high‑resolution stimulation for vision restoration and bidirectional prostheses for naturalistic limb control. Long‑term challenges involve ensuring stable neural integration and minimizing tissue response.

Wearable biosensor systems have advanced rapidly with improvements in flexible electronics and biochemical sensing platforms. These devices enable continuous monitoring of physiological markers such as glucose, lactate, and inflammatory proteins. Future developments target enhanced accuracy, miniaturization, and real‑time clinical feedback.

Machine‑learning‑driven biomarker discovery has accelerated translational research across oncology, neurology, and metabolic diseases. By integrating multi‑omics datasets, computational models can identify candidate molecular signatures associated with disease progression. Robust validation and cross‑cohort generalization remain essential for clinical adoption.
